SOLAR SYSTEM / NEPTUNE

Beyond the familiar.
A distant, windy world.

Cold, distant and windswept. Neptune is the outermost planet, circling the Sun far beyond the warmth of our home world.

Small facts. Big discoveries.

01

Found with mathematics

Astronomers predicted Neptune’s position from disturbances in Uranus’s orbit before identifying it through a telescope in 1846.

02

Wild weather far from the Sun

Neptune’s winds can exceed 2,000 kilometers per hour, making it the windiest planet in our solar system.

03

A moon going against the flow

Triton orbits opposite Neptune’s rotation. This unusual orbit suggests it was captured rather than forming alongside the planet.
